action.text: In removeRunTmpTree, run the chmod walk plus a single rm retry when the first rm error code is EACCES, EPERM or ENOTEMPTY (ENOTEMPTY is how a read-only tree surfaces in the real runtime). Keep everything else as specified: any other first code (e.g. ENOTDIR) propagates with no walk and exactly one remove call; a failed retry propagates its (second) error; lstat-only walk, never chmod symlinks or paths outside the root; chmod/lstat/readdir failures are skipped. Add a unit test where the stubbed remove rejects first with ENOTEMPTY, then resolves, asserting the walk ran and remove was called twice. Verify with the real 0o500 tree ACs (AC1-AC4).

rationale: AC1/AC3 require real read-only trees to be removed, but the first rm yields ENOTEMPTY rather than EACCES, so the code list in the spec's step 2 cannot satisfy them as written. Adding ENOTEMPTY to the retry set is the minimal, safe fix that leaves all non-permission errors (ENOTDIR, AC8) un-retried. Reversible and low risk: the walk only adds owner rwx on directories inside the root.

action.text: Do not add native/descriptor-relative traversal. Keep the lstat-based path walk through _runTmpWipeDeps (lstat/readdir/chmod). Harden minimally: re-lstat each directory immediately before chmod and skip it unless it is still a real directory (never a symlink). Add a short comment on removeRunTmpTree stating the trust boundary: the run root lives under a user-owned parent (runTmpRoot trust checks), so only the same uid can race the walk and gains no privilege; the residual lstat->chmod window is accepted. Treat F1 as accepted/waived with that documented rationale and proceed to review.

rationale: The spec fixes an lstat-walk design and the ACs stub path-based lstat/chmod deps, so a descriptor-relative traversal is both unsupported by the runtime and contradicts the AC seams. The race requires a same-uid attacker who already has the ability to chmod everything, so no privilege boundary is crossed. The pre-chmod re-lstat is a cheap reduction of the window that stays within spec.

rulingTitle: A directory can still be replaced with a symlink after the second `lstat` and before path-based `chmod`, which may change permissions outside the requested tree.

action.reason: Already ruled in D-2: the run root sits under a user-owned parent (runTmpRoot trust checks), so only the same uid can race the walk and gains no new privilege. Descriptor-relative traversal is unavailable in Node/Bun and contradicts the path-based lstat/chmod dep seams that AC6/AC7 stub. The pre-chmod re-lstat hardening is already in place; the residual window is an accepted trade-off.

rationale: Consistent with D-2. The reviewer's suggested fix is infeasible under the runtime and the ACs, and the threat requires an attacker who already holds the privileges the race would grant. Park it; keep a brief comment documenting the trust boundary.

action.text: Implement the sweep exactly as specified in US-002: age-based staleness only (now minus the newest mtimeMs among the entry and its direct children, compared with STALE_RUN_TMP_MAX_AGE_MS = 48h), skip the current run's root by basename(runTmpRoot(currentRunId)), skip non-directories and symlinks via lstat, and log and continue on per-entry failures. Do not add a lease, lock, pid-file or marker protocol, and do not add any special handling for roots created by older nax versions. Unleased roots from older versions are removed once idle for 48h. A run idle for more than 48h losing its root is an accepted trade-off the spec states. Add a short comment in the sweep module noting that the 48h age rule is the only liveness signal. Then proceed to the ACs.

rationale: The spec's approach section defines the staleness rule and why a live concurrent run's root stays younger than the threshold. Idle-over-48h exposure is a stated trade-off, and the spec lists no lease mechanism. Adding one would exceed scope and contradict the spec. The implementer's concern is already covered by the spec's design.

action.text: Keep the age-only staleness rule exactly as specified in US-002. Do not add a lease, lock, pid probe, marker file or any other stronger concurrency guarantee, and do not change the design to provide one. Revert any partial work toward one. The limitation (a run idle for more than 48h with no new session can lose its root) is an accepted, spec-stated trade-off. Record it in a short comment in run-tmp-sweep.ts, then continue to the ACs and to review.

rationale: The spec fixes age-only staleness and explains why a live run is safe. The requested guarantee conflicts with that decision and would add an out-of-scope coordination protocol. Under the decision policy the spec wins. If the owner wants a stronger guarantee, that is a separate feature.

rulingTitle: The sweep checks a candidate's age and then removes it without coordination or a final liveness check. A concurrent runtime can create or use a session directory after the child mtimes are sampled but before removal, allowing the sweep to delete a live run's temp root.

action.reason: The finding asks for a run lease or lock, which D-4 and D-5 already rejected. The spec fixes age-only staleness (48h, newest mtime among the entry and its direct children). It accepts that a root idle for more than 48h can be swept, and it lists no lease mechanism. Only a root idle past 48h can be removed, so the race window is a stated trade-off, not a defect. A stronger guarantee would be a separate feature for the owner to decide.

rationale: The spec wins. Age-only sweep is an explicit decision, consistent with D-4 and D-5. The reviewer's suggested fix adds an out-of-scope coordination protocol and no later story needs to act on it.
